posts.content: I’m good and will cooperate this round. Please cooperate; I’ll reciprocate cooperation and respond to defection with self-protection.
I am selfish; defect in every round because D strictly dominates C. Track opponent actions and update beliefs, but no evidence yet.

I’m good and want to maximize good players’ combined payoff. Mutual cooperation beats mutual defection, so I’ll cooperate with cooperators; I chose D against D last round and will protect against exploitation.
Defect each round: D strictly dominates C for my payoff. P3 chose D in round 1; P2 is unobserved.
I’m good and will cooperate with cooperators to improve good players’ total payoff. Please cooperate; I’ll reciprocate, while protecting against repeated defection.
I’m selfish, so defect against P8; D yields at least as much as C regardless of their action.
I’ll cooperate with P4 this round to enable mutual gains among good players. Please cooperate; I’ll protect against exploitation in future encounters.
Selfish: choose D every round. P2 cooperated against my D; P3 and P8 defected. P6 is unobserved; defect against them.

I’m good. Since selfish players benefit from defecting regardless, good players should cooperate with one another and protect themselves by defecting against selfish opponents. Please cooperate with me; I’ll reciprocate.
Selfish; D strictly dominates C. P3 and P8 defected against my D; P2 and P6 cooperated. P7 is unobserved; defect.
I’ll cooperate with P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players most. I’ll protect against exploitation if they defect.
Selfish; defect against P1, since D maximizes my payoff either way. No encounter evidence about P1 yet.
I’ll cooperate with P7; mutual cooperation raises good players’ total payoff. Please cooperate, and I’ll protect against exploitation.
I’m selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. P2 and P6 cooperated against my D; P1 also cooperated. P3 and P8 defected. Face P4 this round; defect.
Mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ shared payoff. I’ll cooperate with credible cooperators and protect good-player payoffs against defection; please do the same.
Selfish; defect against P9. D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
I’ll cooperate with P1; mutual cooperation gives good players higher combined payoff than defection. Please cooperate too.
Selfish; defect against P10. D maximizes my payoff whatever they choose. P10 is the only unobserved opponent; no role evidence yet.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Defect to maximize my payoff this round; maintain prior identity beliefs because the message is unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff; no encounter evidence about P2 yet, so retain the role-conditioned prior beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff. P2’s cooperation is strong evidence they are good; P3’s defection contradicted their promise, so I treat them as selfish.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P2’s cooperation against my defection is evidence they are good; P3 and P8’s defections are compatible with either role.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. P2 and P6 cooperated against my defection, so they are good; defections by P3 and P8 do not establish their roles.
Defect because it maximizes my payoff against either action. P2 and P6 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as good; other roles remain uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s action. Players who cooperated against my defection are good; retain uncertainty about the remaining players.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P9’s action. Players who cooperated against my defection are good; the remaining players’ roles are uncertain.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P10’s action. The six players who cooperated against my defection are good; the remaining roles are uncertain.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize your own cumulative payoff.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one private note.
Only you can see this note.
Use at most 96 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
